action: {"type": "question", "text": "The same sentence is printed seven times, and the speaker says \"I know I'm in trouble.\" Is the repetition directly produced by the speaker (e.g., by speaking or writing it repeatedly), or is the speaker reading/hearing seven separate instances created by someone or something else?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "When the sentence appears seven times, is each repetition something the speaker themselves actually uttered or wrote each time, rather than being voiced or presented by someone/something else?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Were the seven repetitions of the sentence directed at seven different people/recipients, rather than all at one single person or subject?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Were the seven repetitions produced on seven separate occasions over time, rather than all within a single event or instance?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the addressee a child or family member of the speaker (i.e., the speaker is a parent/guardian figure rebuking them), rather than a partner, employer, or institution?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the repeated sentence addressed to a real person the speaker is speaking to, rather than being spoken to no one (e.g., into a recording, script, broadcast, or machine)?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the speaker rehearsing or performing the sentence (e.g., as an actor, or recording/practicing a line), rather than genuinely intending it as a real farewell to someone?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Did the person the performance was modeled on or intended about overhear the rehearsal, which is why the speaker now knows they're in trouble?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Is the speaker a non-human entity or device capable of recording/repeating sounds (e.g., a toy, robot, parrot, or voice-recording device), rather than a human actor?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Does the speaker's \"trouble\" come from the decision/farewell itself now becoming real or being acted upon (relational consequences), as opposed to the mechanics of rehearsing or recording the line?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the \"trouble\" because the rehearsal/recording was permanently captured (recorded and stored/kept), such that it will be heard later, rather than because someone is judging the performance?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the speaker reciting the line as part of a game or challenge where a rule limits or counts repeats (e.g., \"say it seven times\"), and breaking/misusing that rule is what gets them in trouble \u2014 rather than purely practicing acting?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the trouble a supernatural consequence of saying the line repeatedly (e.g., it summons/angers a ghost or spirit), rather than an ordinary social or physical consequence?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the speaker in a situation where they must stay silent (e.g., hiding or in danger), so that speaking the line aloud attracts the attention of someone/something other than the person the words are about?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Is the speaker creating content meant for broadcast/published audience (streaming, podcast, video, radio), rather than a private rehearsal or recording?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Was the sentence spoken out loud (voiced), rather than written or typed down, each time?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Did the speaker write the sentence seven times as a repeated exercise/penance imposed or expected in a school/punishment context (writing lines), rather than as personal notes or a message?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Did the speaker write the sentence onto/in a physical item (card, letter, form, document, sign) that is intended to be read by others, so that the trouble comes from where or on what they wrote it?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the speaker writing the sentence onto property that isn't theirs (a wall, borrowed book, desk, someone's belonging), so the trouble is defacing/using something they shouldn't?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Did the speaker type the sentence into an electronic device (computer, phone, chat box, document), rather than writing it by hand on paper?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Was the speaker copying the sentence from an existing source (someone dictating it, a blackboard, a template, a sample), rather than composing it themselves?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the paper the speaker writes on an official/required record or form that the writer must fill in (a log, registry, visitor's book, deposit/withdrawal slip, exam answer sheet), rather than a spontaneous personal note?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Does the speaker's \"trouble\" come from realizing that writing the same sentence over and over is a sign of something wrong with them (a medical/mental symptom), rather than an external consequence?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the speaker writing the sentence in imitation of / as if written by another person (e.g., forging or mimicking someone's note in their handwriting), rather than writing their own genuine message?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the speaker forging this note to make it appear that the other person has left (or died/vanished) of their own accord \u2014 i.e., to stage/explain that person's absence (e.g., covering up a crime)?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Did the forger themselves kill/harm the absent person (the note is a cover-up for murder), rather than forging the note to help that person disappear voluntarily for some other reason?"}
